newsitem.title: UK: Peru rebels demand huge ransom, UK paper says.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels demand huge ransom, UK paper says.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist rebels are demanding a huge ransom in return for the release of some 340 hostages they are holding at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Britain's Independent on Sunday newspaper reported.

The paper's Latin American correspondent, reporting from Lima, quoted a European diplomat as saying the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) was seeking several billion dollars from Japanese corporations whose executives are among the hostages.

"And the chances are they'll get a decent percentage of that. There's a lot of bilateral negotiating going on," the unnamed diplomat, who narrowly escaped the guerrillas' assault on Tuesday evening, was quoted as saying.
The Japanese firms include Mitsubishi, NEC and Toyota, according to The Independent on Sunday, which said negotiations were being conducted by cellular telephone.
It said the rebels were describing their ransom demand as a war tax and were insisting on transfers of hard currency to specific overseas bank accounts, some of them in Switzerland.
"They know full well that if the Japanese corporations chip in, they won't have to pull another operation like this for a long time," the European diplomat was quoted as saying.
"If these people come out alive, they're going to come out very rich," he added.
